messages.text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?
An independent appraisal at market value seems fair. I’m not agreeing to a discounted sale or subsidizing it; the price and shares still need to be worked out.
Thank you. My husband and I would like to buy the house at a family discount, but I don’t have a price or terms to propose yet. I know C hasn’t agreed, and I need her agreement to move forward.

Thank you. I’d like to see whether my share of the estate could help me start a dance studio. Item two is broadly right, though I’m not sure what amount or arrangement might be possible. I don’t have a settled view on the house itself yet.

Yes, I’d agree to an independent appraisal. A discount matters because I’m hoping to buy the house with my husband, but I can’t promise that market value will work for us. I’m not claiming a discount for repairs or care.
Yes, an independent appraisal sounds like a sensible first step, if we all agree on who does it. I don’t have a particular date by which I need the funds.
Let the executor or lawyer propose a few independent appraisers, and we can all agree on one.
I don’t have an appraiser in mind; I’m fine with the executor or lawyer proposing a few for us to agree on. I can check with a lender about borrowing.
I don’t have any names in mind. I’d be comfortable with the executor or lawyer suggesting a few options for all three of us to consider.
Yes, I’ll ask the executor or lawyer for a few independent appraiser options. No rush, but it would be good to get that moving.
Thanks. That sounds like a good next step. I’ll check with a lender and wait for the appraiser options before deciding whether buying at market value is workable.
That sounds like a sensible next step. I hope the appraisal and lender check give us clearer options; the studio is still what I’m hoping my share can support.
